description: Relax, reset, and reconnect through soothing sound vibrations designed to quiet the mind, release tension, and restore your energy.
long_description:
Relax, reset, and reconnect through soothing sound vibrations designed to quiet the mind, release tension, and restore your energy.

About this Event

Yoga Flow + Sound Bath ✨Take a moment to slow down, move, breathe, and reconnect with yourself. Join us for an evening of gentle movement and deep relaxation featuring a yoga flow followed by an immersive sound bath experience.
Whether you’re new to yoga and sound baths or already love them, this experience is designed to give you space to unwind, release tension, and simply be present.

What to Bring 🧘🏽‍♀️Yoga matBlanket, pillow, eye mask, or anything else that helps you feel cozy and comfortable during the sound bath (optional)An open mind and a willingness to relax ✨Come as you are, get comfortable, and give yourself permission to slow down.
Space is limited so get your tickets soon!

Agenda

Check-In & Settle In
Info: Arrive, check in, set up your mat, get comfortable, and place your smoothie order if you’d like one. Smoothies will be prepared after the session.

Yoga Flow + Sound Bath
Host: Alex
Info: We’ll begin with a guided yoga flow to help you move, stretch, and connect with your breath before transitioning into a relaxing sound bath. Allow the soothing sounds and vibrations to create a peaceful space for rest and reflection.

Sound Bowl Presentation + Smoothies
Info: Learn more about the sound bowls and their unique sounds and vibrations while pre-ordered and new smoothie orders are prepared. Stay, enjoy your smoothie, and ease out of the experience at your own pace.

Also check out other in Raleigh, Health & Wellness events in Raleigh.

title: Quick & Easy Indian Cooking
description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

long_description:
Step away from the noise of everyday life and give yourself permission to slow down. Our Women’s Refresh, Reset & Relaxation Retreat is a thoughtfully curated multi-day experience designed to help you recharge, reconnect, and indulge in simple joys. Spend your days moving gently, nourishing your body, enjoying meaningful conversation, and embracing unstructured time to do exactly what makes you happy — whether that’s lounging by the pool, reading a book, or treating yourself to a massage.

From yoga to afternoon tea, Italian cooking night, and a lively murder mystery dinner, this immersive, multi-day experience blends wellness, creativity, and indulgence to help you recharge—mind, body, and spirit.

________________________________________

✨ Day 1: Arrival & Welcome

Ease into the weekend at your own pace. Arrive between 4:00–7:00 PM and settle in with pool time, light bites, and a curated charcuterie spread.

At 7:00 PM, we’ll gather in the dining room for a relaxed, build-your-own salad dinner. Enjoy meaningful introductions and guided intention setting to ground your experience and connect with fellow guests.

The evening winds down as the first floor closes at 9:30 PM, inviting you into restful stillness.

________________________________________

🌿 Day 2: Restore & Indulge

Begin your morning with coffee, tea, fresh fruit, or a smoothie before an 8:30 AM yoga session.

After breakfast, the day unfolds with a balance of scheduled treatments and free time. Enjoy massages and/or facials throughout the day—offered in the library or out on the pool deck in the privacy of a secluded space—while also having time to relax however you choose. Lounge by the pool, unwind on the front porch, curl up with a book, or take a peaceful walk to the nearby Cincinnati Zoo.

Midday brings a vibrant taco bar lunch, followed by late afternoon tea with light bites served either in the parlor or poolside.

title: Navratri 2026 - Live Garba And Dandiya Night By Pancham Beats
description: Light Up the Night at Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night by Pancham Beats
long_description:
Light Up the Night at Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night by Pancham Beats
Mark your calendars for the 15th of October, 2026, as Pancham Beats LLC brings you an unforgettable night of celebration and dance at the Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night. Experience the joy of Navratri, one of the most vibrant festivals celebrated with great fervor and enthusiasm. Lose yourself in the rhythmic beats of Garba and Dandiya, traditional dance forms from the Indian state of Gujarat. description: A gentle, grounding yoga practice influenced by Yin & Restorative Yoga, designed to slow down, release tension, and reconnect.
long_description:
A gentle, grounding yoga practice influenced by Yin & Restorative Yoga, designed to slow down, release tension, and reconnect.

About this Event

Chill Yoga with Jason is a gentle, grounding practice designed to help you slow down, reconnect, and settle into the present moment.
Heavily influenced by Yin and Restorative Yoga, Jason will guide a steady, unhurried flow incorporating longer-held shapes, intentional stillness, and supported postures to encourage release, relaxation, and deeper awareness of the body.
The practice is spacious and grounding, with an emphasis on mindful pacing, intentional movement, and creating a sense of calm both on and off the mat. Options and modifications will be offered throughout, making the class welcoming for both newer students and experienced yogis alike.
This is a donation-based class, with a portion of proceeds benefiting the NW Community Food Bank and Van Ness Main Street, helping support the organizations and community that make these gatherings possible.
Please bring your own mat. Some props will be provided, though you are welcome to bring any additional props you prefer, such as blocks, straps, or blankets.
As part of Yoga on Connecticut, our community yoga project, we're excited to continue creating opportunities for neighbors to gather through movement, mindfulness, and meaningful connection.
Plan to arrive a few minutes early to settle in and set up your space before class begins.

description: REZN
long_description:
REZN – the Chicago-based band of Rob McWilliams (vocals, guitar), Phil Cangelosi (bass), Patrick Dunn (drums), and Spencer Ouellette (synth/saxophone) – announce their new album, Burden, out June 14th via their new label Sargent House. In conjunction, they present its massive lead single/video, “Chasm.” Since their inception, REZN have mined the stark monochromatic depths of underground metal and fused them with the kaleidoscopic delights of psychedelia, prog rock, and shoegaze. With their latest album Burden, they plumb the deepest, bleakest trenches of their sound while retaining a lifeline into the cosmos. Staking a claim at the crossroads of the hazy dimensions of modern psych acts like Black Angels, the cavernous gloom and reverb-drenched guitar of bands like Spectral Voice, and the lurching low-end meditations of artists like OM, REZN have created Burden—an album of immense amp-worshipping weight and intoxicating instrumentation.

Burden was recorded simultaneously with their previous album Solace back in July 2021 at Earth Analog Studios in Tolono, IL by Matt Russell. Rather than release a double album, REZN divided the material into two separate records, each with its own distinct emotional timbre. Whereas Solace was meant to uplift and create a sense of narcotic dreaminess, Burden skews towards the themes of delirium, claustrophobia, and misery. Musically, Burden favors riffs over atmosphere, percussion over ether, dissonance over beauty, but there is still an undeniable cohesion between it and its predecessor. The marriage of brute force and sublime textures has always been a key tactic in REZN’s approach—a duality that may explain their touring history with fellow synesthesia-inducing metallurgists Elder and Russian Circles—but the spectrum of the band’s mercurial temperaments has never felt as clearly defined and fully explored as it does on Burden.

Experience the Soulful Melodies with Rahat Fateh Ali Khan in Houston

Known for his profound Ghazals, enchanting Qawwali, and soul-stirring Sufi songs, Rahat Fateh Ali Khan is all set to perform live at the 'Voice of Peace' concert. This event promises an evening filled with Hindi music, live in concert, that is sure to leave the audience spellbound.
Meet the Maestro: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan
Belonging to a family of traditional musicians, Rahat Fateh Ali Khan carries forward the legacy of his renowned musical lineage. Famous for his melodious voice, Rahat has captivated audiences globally with hits like 'Teri Meri' from the movie Bodyguard. His unique ability to blend traditional Sufi music with contemporary sounds has made him a beloved figure in the international music scene. Witness the magic of his voice and be a part of an unforgettable musical journey.
Delight in the Ambiance of Reliant Arena
The concert will be held at the well-known Reliant Arena, located at One Reliant Park, Houston, TX, United States. Known for its state-of-the-art facilities and stellar acoustics, the Reliant Arena ensures a safe and enjoyable concert experience. Its easy accessibility and abundant parking make it a preferred choice for concert-goers. After the concert, explore the vibrant city of Houston and indulge in some delicious Indian cuisine at nearby restaurants.

long_description:
Experience the Vibrant Pulse of Navratri at GCA Bay Area Ras Garba
Join us on the 17th of October, 2026 as the Gujarati Cultural Association of the Bay Area presents the GCA Bay Area Ras Garba. This event will be a unique blend of Gujarati and Multilingual music and dance, a cultural extravaganza that brings the traditional Navratri/Dandiya celebration to life. Be prepared to groove to the rhythmic beats and mesmerizing tunes put together by the talented Aanal & Achal Anjaria Team from Sharda Musical Group.
Meet the Maestros: Aanal & Achal Anjaria
Although there's no specific artist announced for this event, the GCA Bay Area Ras Garba is meticulously curated by the Aanal & Achal Anjaria Team from Sharda Musical Group. This team is renowned for their passion and dedication towards preserving and promoting Gujarati culture through music. They are sure to deliver an unforgettable experience with their vibrant rhythms and captivating melodies that will keep you dancing all night long.
Fremont's Cultural Hotspot: Washington High School
The GCA Bay Area Ras Garba will be held at Washington High School, located at 38442 Boulevard, Fremont, CA, United States. Known for its safe and accessible location, the venue promises an enjoyable and hassle-free experience for all attendees. The area boasts a number of Indian restaurants, perfect for those looking to indulge in some authentic cuisine before or after the event. Parking is available on-site, ensuring your convenience.
Secure Your Place: Ticket Information
Don't miss out on this unique cultural experience. We offer General Admission tickets at $25.00, ensuring everyone can partake in the fun. If you're planning to come along with a group, take advantage of our special offer for groups of 8 or more, with tickets priced at just $23.00. Grab your tickets now and get ready to immerse yourself in the vibrant world of Gujarati music and dance at the GCA Bay Area Ras Garba.

Mark your calendar for the 17th of October, 2026, as the rhythm of Dandiya beats fill the air in Cupertino. The San Jose | Cupertino Dandiya Nite, brought to you by Net Effect Media, promises an unforgettable evening of Punjabi, Hindi, Telugu, Gujarati and English music, delicious food and drink, and the pulsating energy of Navratri. Whether you're a Bollywood enthusiast or just looking for a great night party, this event brings the vibrant spirit of Navratri to life.
Unveiling the Night with Remarkable Artists
While we're keeping the artists under wraps for now, rest assured that the performers of the night will captivate you with their stellar renditions of various Indian regional music. Their enchanting performances in Punjabi, Hindi, Telugu, and Gujarati will transport you to the heart of India, and their English tunes will have you swaying in rhythm. Stay tuned for more updates!
Cherishing the Night at Marriott Residence Inn
Located at 19429 Stevens Creek Blvd, the Marriott Residence Inn in Cupertino, CA, United States, is a venue that perfectly matches the grandeur of our event. The location is well-regarded for its safety, accessibility, and the variety of attractions nearby. Parking won't be an issue as the venue has ample space for your convenience. What's more, the surrounding area is dotted with Indian restaurants, perfect for those who wish to continue the night with some delicious Indian cuisine.
Securing your Spot at the Dandiya Nite
You wouldn't want to miss this night of fun, dance, and music. Grab your tickets now! Our Early Bird offer gets you a Single Ticket for $24.00, 4 Tickets for $89.00, and 10 Tickets for $199.00. If you missed the Early Bird offer, worry not. Regular tickets are available at $26.00 for a Single Ticket, $96.00 for 4 Tickets, and $220.00 for 10 Tickets. Creator of The Phoenix Practice™

Dr. Shelley Best (RYT-200) is a yoga teacher, mindfulness meditation teacher, sound practitioner, and creator of The Phoenix Practice™. Her path began at West Hartford Yoga, where - only a few classes in - a middle-of-the-night calling sent her to India within two and a half weeks. At the ashram of Sri Mata Amritanandamayi - Amma, "the hugging saint" - in Kerala, she immersed in Amrita Yoga and the Integrated Amrita Meditation technique under Amma's personal guidance. India is where her own healing began.

She carried that healing home.

title: Ayurveda for Fall: Yoga, Nourishment + Seasonal Self-Care
description: Fall Ayurveda + yoga to calm your nervous system, nourish your body and discover seasonal practices to help you feel more balanced.
long_description:
Fall Ayurveda + yoga to calm your nervous system, nourish your body and discover seasonal practices to help you feel more balanced.

About this Event

As the days grow shorter and the air turns crisp, we often feel an inner shift. In Ayurveda, fall is known as Vata season - a time defined by the energy of wind, movement, and change.
When this energy rises in the natural world, it can show up within us as an unsettled mind, restless sleep, joint discomfort, dry skin, or irregular digestion.
This seasonal shift is also an invitation to slow down, nourish yourself, and create more stability. Ayurveda offers time-honored practices to help support the body and nervous system as we move from summer into fall.
Join Michele for a seasonal Ayurveda and yoga workshop designed to help you move through fall feeling grounded, replenished, and warmed from the inside out.

WHAT WE’LL EXPLORE:Movement:
A slow, centering yoga practice for fall with an emphasis on calming the nervous system, releasing tension from the hips and spine, and using the breath as a steady anchor.
Nourishment:
Ayurvedic principles for maintaining vitality through warming seasonal foods, soothing self-care rituals, and daily habits that support greater stability as the season deepens.

WHAT YOU’LL LEAVE WITH:A short home yoga practice and approachable Ayurvedic self-care rituals you can return to throughout the fall season.
When the world outside feels blustery and unpredictable, you’ll have practices to help you reconnect with what feels steady within, leaving you feeling nourished, centered, and with a deeper understanding of what brings you back into balance.
No previous experience with Ayurveda or yoga is necessary.

Pépin Lecture Series - Safar with Madhushree Ghosh
description: Join Madhushree Ghosh as she discusses her book, Safar: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West!
long_description:
Join Madhushree Ghosh as she discusses her book, Safar: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West!

About this Event

This event will be live steamed on Zoom. You can select an in-person or virtual ticket. Virtual ticket holders will receive a Zoom link prior to the event.

Madhushree Ghosh (Phd in biochemistry) is the author of Khabaar: An Immigrant Journey of Food, Memory and Family and SAFAR: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West. She is the creative founder of KhabaarCo, a global literary salon and supper club. As a TEDx Speaker, Madhushree interrogates cultural, culinary and immigration issues using food as a social justice tool.

Published in June of this year, Safar blends memoir and history to explore the role of Punjabi food in fostering community and identity among South Asian refugees and immigrants.

Safar follows the journey of South Asian refugees, immigrants, and their children-in particular, Sikhs, Jats, and Muslims-who moved to the southwestern states of America over centuries as farmers, truck drivers, restaurant owners, and dhaba/diner stall cooks. An expedition in search of the asli-or real Punjabi food-Madhushree Ghosh explores how their food traveled from pre-partition British India to now, while weaving in her own immigrant journey as a graduate student to America in 1993, her quest to find home through the food of her Bengali refugee parents, and the physical journey she embarked on to visit the Punjabi communities in California, Arizona, and New Mexico.

Focusing on four Punjabi women, each a part of a different immigration wave of South Asia to the American West, Ghosh highlights the food and recipes they brought with them that connect them to their pasts. Safar shares stories of displacement, discrimination, community, and hope, while shedding light on immigrant journeys and the true meaning of home, comfort food, and what constitutes a “true Punjabi” meal. Diwali and Navratri are my favorite holidays and are heavily celebrated in my family bringing us luck, good faith, and joy. long_description:
Now in its 13th year, Diwali on the Hudson returns as one of New York City's largest and most anticipated Diwali celebrations. What began as an intimate community gathering has grown into a sold-out, flagship annual event, welcoming friends, professionals, creatives, and changemakers for an unforgettable night honoring the Festival of Lights, while supporting the transformative work of the Desai Foundation.

Hosted at HK Hall in the heart of Hell's Kitchen, the evening blends culture, celebration, and impact through live entertainment, Indian food, dancing, and meaningful connection with a vibrant community. Over the years, the event has welcomed celebrities, influencers, and community leaders, earning recognition from outlets including Good Morning America.

More than a party, Diwali on the Hudson is a space to gather in joy and intention, celebrating culture while learning how the Desai Foundation empowers women and children across rural India through health, livelihood, and menstrual equity programs.

About this Event

As we step into the 20th year of our Durga Puja, it’s mandatory that we look back and observe many obstacles we have overcome, how we have managed funds, and how we keep organizing the biggest event in our Bengali Culture, mostly how we have become a big joint family. For us, people of BIC, the walls of MM Thompson Room has become the bamboo pandal, the drawings and stuffs made by our decoration team have became the chandelier of Naktala Udayan Sangha, the YouTube Red “dhaak” music has became our real dhaki, sometimes a little snow didn’t stop us to believe that we are enjoying the Sarotkal, like Apu-Durga, we are also chasing though the kaashful and trying to soak up every bit of it. Such power holds this event, such is the power of Maa Durga! অশুভ শক্তির বিনাস, triumph over evil, she make us believe in ourselves, the truth and strength. title: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening
description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? How can one live with intelligence and clarity? If all existence is One, why do we perceive differences? What is the nature of the universe and its origin? How can we understand the cause of the universe? How does one transcend the sense of limitation? title: Quick & Easy Indian Cooking
description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

description: San Diego, this one's for you. Desi Comedy Fest, the biggest South Asian comedy festival in America
long_description:
San Diego, this one's for you. Desi Comedy Fest, the biggest South Asian comedy festival in America

About this Event

San Diego, this one's for you. Desi Comedy Fest, the biggest South Asian comedy festival in America, brings its SoCal Tour to the Gaslamp for one night only.
Our mission is simple: showcase the funniest comedians of South Asian heritage from around the globe and create a live comedy experience unlike anything else. Six to eight comedians share one stage, back to back, for two hours of nonstop laughs.
The lineup celebrates the full diversity of the diaspora: Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, Nepali and beyond. From Bollywood to brown parents to growing up between two cultures, this is comedy that hits different when the whole room gets the joke.
And everybody's invited, no translation needed. Featured on NBC, CBS, Just For Laughs and SF Sketchfest, the Fest has sold out rooms across America for over a decade, with comedians who have been part of Netflix Is A Joke, launched specials on Amazon and HBO, and appeared on late night from Letterman to Conan.
Saturday November 7 it finally lands in San Diego at National Lampoon: The Yellow Door.
Come see why 20,000 people have made this the night they plan their week around.

long_description:
Join Heather Burkart, eRYT500, on Sunday November 8th from 9:00am-5:00pm at Healium Hot Yoga-Bay View’s Cozy Studio for a full-day intensive focused on meditation as a personalized practice.

Meditation is not a one-size-fits-all practice. This immersive workshop explores traditional and modern meditation techniques through the Ayurvedic lens, helping participants discover practices that align with their unique constitution and current state of balance. Through guided experiences, discussion, and self-inquiry, students will develop practical tools for cultivating focus, resilience, self-awareness, and inner calm while gaining confidence in guiding meditation practices for others. Class will not be hot/heated. 

$125 early bird pricing - sign up by November 1st

$150 full price - after November 1st

description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

description: Get ready to dance the night away with silent beats from Bollywood to Tollywood and all the cool vibes underneath the stary night!
long_description:
Get ready to dance the night away with silent beats from Bollywood to Tollywood and all the cool vibes underneath the stary night!

About this Event

Headphones on, Austin. Bollywood, Tollywood and everything in between, at The Domain, Amy Donovan Plaza.
Overview
When the sun goes down on Panchabhootam, the plaza turns into a dance floor.
Join SAIVA on Saturday, November 14, from 8:30 to 9:30 PM for a silent disco at The Domain's Amy Donovan Plaza. Bollywood, Tollywood, and everything in between, playing straight into your headphones under the open Texas sky.
This is the closing celebration of Panchabhootam, SAIVA's festival of the five great elements: earth, water, fire, air and space. All afternoon, the elements come alive through the senses. The silent disco ends the day with sound, the sense of space, and everyone dancing together.
At SAIVA, we believe every generation has something to give and something to learn. So bring your grandmother, your kids, your college roommate and your neighbors. Some of our best dancers have been practicing in our weekly classes since May.
How it works
When you arrive, you'll pick up a pair of wireless headphones. 3 channels each play a different mix, and the light on your headset shows which one you're tuned to, so you can find the people dancing to your song.
Want to talk? Slide one ear off. No shouting over speakers, and no ringing ears on the drive home. It's the most social way to dance.
Make a day of it
Come early for the free Panchabhootam festival from 3 to 6 PM at the same plaza:
Experience the elementsDance performancesSeed ball creation, art, and fermentation activitiesFood for purchase and a marketFamily activities for all agesGood to know

title: Special Program: Counter-Histories—Memory, Materiality & South Asian Art
description: Syona Puliady and UCLA Arts Dean Lionel Popkin discuss South Asian art, material, memory, and reimagined histories.
long_description:
Syona Puliady and UCLA Arts Dean Lionel Popkin discuss South Asian art, material, memory, and reimagined histories.

About this Event

Curator of Textiles of the Eastern Hemisphere Syona Puliady will join UCLA Dean of the School of the Arts and Architecture Lionel Popkin for a conversation on the themes underlying Textiles as Monument and Field Notes from Begumpura: memory, materiality, and the creation of alternative histories through contemporary art.

By focusing on the works of Suchitra Mattai, Jagdeep Raina, Swapnaa Tamhane, and Rahee Punyashloka, Puliady and Popkin will consider how artists use textiles, speculative storytelling, archival practices, and other forms of cultural expression to challenge dominant narratives and center communities whose histories have often been overlooked. Together, they will address how contemporary South Asian artists create new forms of remembrance, belonging, and possibility through material and imagined worlds.

Lionel Popkin is the dean of the UCLA School of the Arts and Architecture and a professor of choreography in the UCLA Department of World Arts and Cultures/Dance. He previously served as the school’s associate dean for academic affairs (2021–24) and chair of the World Arts and Cultures/Dance department (2015–18). Popkin’s artistic practice engages people, objects, and media to explore hybridity, archival practices, and the complexities of representing the South Asian diaspora in North America. His performance and video artworks have been presented at leading cultural venues on four continents, and his written works have been included in scholarly journals and arts publications. He joined UCLA's faculty in 2006 and is a resident artist at the 18th Street Arts Center.

Syona Puliady is curator of textiles of the Eastern Hemisphere at the Fowler Museum. Her research focuses on histories and textiles of the Indian Ocean realm. Her work also takes her to the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu, where she collaborates with art

description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? How can one live with intelligence and clarity? If all existence is One, why do we perceive differences? What is the nature of the universe and its origin? How can we understand the cause of the universe? How does one transcend the sense of limitation? This comprehensive study covers: The nature of the Self (Atman) and Reality (Brahman) Self-knowledge that includes dozens of methods to reveal your nature The role of karma, dharma, and free will The nature of the mind and consciousness (or awareness) The art of wise living and decision-making Cultivating emotional maturity and inner peace Through this course, you will: Grasp the core teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and their relevance to modern life Apply practical techniques for refining your thinking and mastering your emotions Develop a deeper understanding of your identity and the world Cultivate inner peace, clarity, and purpose This knowledge offers a step-by-step method to liberate the seeker from the confines of the ego, from the limitations imposed by the material world, and from the cycle of rebirth. long_description:
Millennial Events presents Ghayal, a brand-new Hindi stand-up comedy show by Pranit More.

In Ghayal, Pranit takes audiences through the journey of his life—the people, places, relationships, and unexpected incidents that have shaped his personality and the way he sees the world. From growing up and navigating everyday life to the unforgettable moments that made headlines, Pranit brings his experiences to the stage through candid storytelling, sharp observations, and his distinctive comedic style.

Personal, honest, and packed with humour, Ghayal offers audiences a closer look at the stories behind the comedian. Whether they have followed Pranit’s journey for years or are seeing him perform live for the first time, audiences can expect an entertaining evening filled with stories, surprises, and stand-up comedy.

Whether you’re planning a night out with friends, family, or attending solo, this high-energy live performance promises nonstop entertainment and moments you’ll be talking about long after the show ends. If you’re looking to unwind and enjoy quality comedy, you won’t want to miss this show.

New York City's #1 live South Asian comedy dating show.

About this Event

Garam Masala : #1 Desi Dating Show
Sunday December 6, 2026
Showtime 6:30PM, Doors 6PM
Running time 80 minutes

How the Night WorksImagine The Bachelor meets Indian Matchmaking, but live on stage hosted by two comedians who are deeply unqualified and absolutely thriving.
Garam Masala Dating is NYC's #1 live desi dating show where South Asian singles go on a blind date in front of a packed house. Our hosts Surbhi and Wyatt guide the chaos with stand-up, crowd work, and genuine matchmaking instincts. Every show ends with a singles mixer where the audience gets to continue the experiment.
Whether you're South Asian or not, curious, single, coupled up, or just need a story, this is the most fun you'll have watching two people fall in love (or spectacularly not) in real time.

title: Quick & Easy Indian Cooking
description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

title: San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
description: Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
long_description:
Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
Mark your calendars for December 31st, 2026, as on this day, the San Diego Tamil Sangam will host its highly anticipated Annual Membership event. A cultural extravaganza that celebrates the richness and diversity of Tamil heritage, this event is a golden opportunity for Tamil enthusiasts to come together and revel in the vibrancy of this ancient culture. The event is sure to be a hub of engagement, enrichment, and entertainment that fosters the promotion and preservation of Tamil language, arts, and literature.
Artist: A Secret Yet to be Revealed
The event is yet to announce its artist, but it's known for featuring renowned individuals from the Tamil community who have significantly influenced the preservation and promotion of Tamil culture. The mystery guest, no doubt, will offer a memorable experience, showcasing the beauty of Tamil arts and literature that resonates with the audience and deepens their appreciation for this rich culture.
Immerse Yourself in Tamil Culture in the Heart of San Diego
The event takes place in San Diego, California, specifically at the 750 B Street location. The venue is in an easily accessible area of the city, known for its safety and proximity to a variety of attractions. After the event, guests can explore the city's vibrant nightlife, historical landmarks, and breathtaking beaches. And for those craving authentic Indian cuisine, there are numerous Indian restaurants nearby where you can indulge in a variety of flavorful dishes.
Secure Your Membership: Ticket Information
Various membership options are available for purchase, ensuring there's something for everyone. The Annual Family Membership is priced at $60.00, providing an excellent opportunity for families to be part of the Tamil community in San Diego. The Annual Individual Membership is available for $35.00, perfect for individuals passionate about Tamil culture. Additionally, the Student Membership from India is priced at a discounted rate of $10.00. For those who want to make a long-term commitment, the Lifetime Membership is available for $500.00. Make sure to secure your membership and be part of the San Diego Tamil Sangam's thriving community.

long_description:
Usama Siddiquee is a Bengali-American stand-up comedian, writer, and actor based in New York City. He is currently a finalist on Kevin Hart’s Funny AF for Netflix, which premiered on April 20. In 2024, he made his late-night debut on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, and in 2025 released his first half-hour special with Don’t Tell Comedy on YouTube. The special highlights his signature high-energy, rapid-fire style, with material ranging from growing up Muslim in Texas to dating misadventures and even getting kicked off America’s Got Talent.

As an actor, Usama has appeared in Netflix’s Inventing Anna and Survival of the Thickest, HBO’s And Just Like That, Comedy Central’s Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens, and FX’s Better Things. He recently wrapped a supporting role in the upcoming Netflix comedy Best of the Best, alongside Hasan Minhaj, Priyanka Kedia, and Maitreyi Ramakrishnan.

Usama was named a New Face at the prestigious Just For Laughs Festival in 2018. In 2020, he reached the semifinals of America’s Got Talent and appeared in the ABC Discovers Talent Showcase. A decorated festival performer, he was a finalist in the 2017 New York’s Funniest competition at Caroline’s and the NBC Stand-Up competition, and has won top honors at the Laughing Devil Cup Comedy Festival (2016), Yonkers Comedy Festival (2015), and Make Me Laugh Albany Comedy Festival (2015). His work has also been featured by NBC, BuzzFeed, Refinery29, The Scene, Mic.com, FusionTV, and The Huffington Post.
